description: Complete EOS data model: every entity, relationship, constraint, enum, index, and migration path across all three schema surfaces (GitHub main, Beast feature/company-system, UMH platform).

schema_surfaces.summary: EOS data lives across three separate schema surfaces that must be unified. Each surface was authored independently and serves a different layer of the architecture.

surfaces.table_count: 6 core + generated layer (21 storage modules with additional schemas)
surfaces.note: Beast branch not on VPS. Table details inferred from Phase 14.4 inventory: 21 generated storage modules (activity, auth, capabilities, companies, conversations, departments, kpis, login, logout, me, notifications, onboarding, portfolios, preferences, read, readAll, register, roles, steps, tasks, workflows) imply corresponding tables.

surfaces.auth_model: N/A (platform layer, auth handled by middleware)

surfaces.note: Read/write typed Python wrappers over the same Neon tables defined in GitHub main schema.ts. This is NOT a separate schema -- it accesses the same tables. Single coupling point between UMH substrate and EOS data.

entities.name: Users
entities.description: The human operator/principal who owns and governs portfolios, entities, and business operations. The ultimate authority in the EOS hierarchy.

divergence.auth_fields: GitHub has password+firebase_uid (Passport.js+Firebase); UMH has neither (Clerk external)
divergence.resolution: UMH platform schema is the target. Clerk handles auth externally. Profile fields (avatar, full_name, preferences) move to a user_profiles table or Clerk metadata. password and firebase_uid are dropped.

relationships.description: One user can own multiple organizations
One user can be a member of multiple organizations
User is implicit owner via agent assignments
User owns OAuth tokens for integrations

entities.name: Portfolios
entities.description: Strategic container grouping related entities under unified governance and reporting. Represents a coherent economic strategy (e.g., 'tech ventures', 'real estate holdings').

fields.name: user_id
constraints: REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL

relationships.description: Each portfolio belongs to one user
One portfolio contains multiple entities (desired state -- Entities table does not yet exist)

entities.name: Organizations
entities.description: Multi-tenant organization container. Maps to an Entity in the EOS hierarchy (an LLC, C-Corp, or other legal vehicle). Organizations own agents, approvals, outcomes, and sessions.

fields.name: portfolio_id
constraints: REFERENCES portfolios(id) ON DELETE SET NULL

fields_needed.name: entity_type
fields_needed.description: LLC, C-Corp, SPV, Holding Company, etc. from entity_types taxonomy

relationships.description: Each organization can belong to one portfolio

entities.name: OrgMembers
entities.description: Junction table mapping users to organizations with role-based access.

entities.name: Agents
entities.description: AI agents with defined roles, departments, hierarchy, and behavioral configuration. Agents operate within the EOS communication delegation chain.

relationships.description: Agent can be assigned to multiple tasks
Agent can be assigned to deals
Agent can have a parent agent (parent_agent_id)

entities.name: Tasks
entities.description: Work items that can be assigned to agents or humans. Support subtasks, collaboration, and delegation patterns.

fields_needed.name: workflow_id
fields_needed.description: Link to parent workflow if task is a workflow step

fields_needed.name: recurrence_rule
fields_needed.description: RRULE for recurring tasks (e.g., morning brief daily at 7am)

relationships.description: Task can be subtask of parent (parent_task_id)

entities.name: Messages
entities.description: Agent conversation messages. Supports multi-agent conversations with task context and cross-references.

entities.name: AiMessages
entities.description: Separate table for AI assistant (copilot) conversation messages, distinct from agent-to-agent messages.
entities.note: In desired state, AI messages should merge into a unified Messages table with a thread_type discriminator (agent_conversation, ea_chat, copilot) rather than maintaining two separate message tables.

entities.name: CrmContacts
entities.description: Leads, prospects, customers, and churned contacts. Core CRM entity for pipeline management.

fields_needed.name: source
fields_needed.description: Lead source (instagram/referral/event/organic/paid) -- used in OutreachWorkflow qualification

fields_needed.name: age_range
fields_needed.description: Target demographic range -- used in OutreachWorkflow qualification

fields_needed.name: engagement_score
fields_needed.description: Engagement level 0-100 -- used in OutreachWorkflow qualification

relationships.description: One contact can have multiple deals
One contact can have multiple activities (via related_to_type=contact)

entities.name: CrmDeals
entities.description: Pipeline deals with stage progression, value tracking, and probability scoring.

fields_needed.name: product_line
fields_needed.description: Which product/offer this deal is for

relationships.description: One deal can have multiple activities (via related_to_type=deal)

entities.name: CrmActivities
entities.description: CRM interaction log: emails, calls, meetings, tasks, and notes related to contacts or deals.

entities.name: AgentActions
entities.description: Governed agent actions with approval workflow, retry logic, and execution tracking. Central to the EOS governance model.

entities.name: AgentMetrics
entities.description: Daily agent performance snapshots: messages, tasks completed, actions executed, token usage, cost, and time saved.

entities.name: Integrations
entities.description: External service integration registry (Gmail, calendar, etc.).
entities.note: Missing user_id and org_id -- not multi-tenant. Global integration registry without ownership scoping.

entities.name: Notifications
entities.description: User notification system for task assignments, agent events, and integration status changes.

entities.name: Documents
entities.description: Document storage for SOPs, notes, strategy docs, and generated content.

entities.name: Folders
entities.description: Hierarchical folder structure for document organization. Self-referential for nested folders.

entities.name: OauthTokens
entities.description: OAuth token storage for external service integrations (Gmail, etc.).
entities.security_note: access_token and refresh_token stored as plaintext. Must encrypt at rest before production deployment.

entities.name: UserAgentSessions
entities.description: Tracks which agent is currently active for a user within an organization. Enables agent context switching.

entities.name: Approvals
entities.description: Governance approval queue. Agent actions that exceed permission tiers queue here for operator review.

fields.name: resolved_by
constraints: REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL

entities.note: Parallel to agent_actions.requires_approval in GitHub main schema. These two approval systems must be unified -- agent_actions tracks the action lifecycle while approvals provides the governance gate.

entities.name: UmhOutcomes
entities.description: Audit trail for UMH integration outcomes. Records every signal processing result with severity and payload.

entities.name: Embeddings
entities.description: Vector embeddings for semantic search and knowledge graph queries. Uses pgvector extension.

entities_not_yet_in_schema.name: Entities
entities_not_yet_in_schema.description: Legal/operational vehicles (LLC, C-Corp, SPV, etc.) through which economic activity is conducted. The structural wrapper that owns bank accounts, signs contracts, and files taxes. This is the level between Portfolio and Business in the EOS hierarchy.
entities_not_yet_in_schema.note: Currently, 'organizations' in UMH_PLATFORM partially fills this role but lacks entity_type, jurisdiction, compliance fields. The ontology defines 8 entity types (LLC, C-Corp, Holding Company, SPV, Real Estate Entity, Investment Entity, Operating Company, Asset Holding Entity) that have no schema representation.

entities_not_yet_in_schema.name: Departments
entities_not_yet_in_schema.description: Organizational departments with agent assignments, permission tiers, roles, metrics, and workflow references. Currently defined only in Python code (projections/eos/entities.py) with no DB table.
entities_not_yet_in_schema.note: 10 departments defined in code (Executive, Sales, Marketing, Finance, Customer Success, HR, Legal, Operations, Product, Engineering). Beast branch has departments storage module implying a table exists there.

entities_not_yet_in_schema.name: Roles
entities_not_yet_in_schema.description: Named permission/responsibility sets for humans and agents. Currently defined only in Python code (projections/eos/entities.py). Beast branch has roles storage module.

entities_not_yet_in_schema.name: Workflows
entities_not_yet_in_schema.description: Executable process definitions with steps, triggers, governance gates, and automation levels. Currently defined in Python code (projections/eos/entities.py) and 3 Python workflow implementations. Beast branch has workflows storage module and workflows page.
entities_not_yet_in_schema.note: 10 workflows defined in entities.py code (Morning Brief, Outreach Sequence, Content Calendar, Expense Review, Ticket Routing, Hiring Pipeline, Contract Review, Incident Response, Feature Prioritization, Code Review & Deploy). 3 implemented as Python classes (Outreach, Content, FollowUp).

entities_not_yet_in_schema.name: WorkflowRuns
entities_not_yet_in_schema.description: Execution instances of workflows. Tracks each run through step completion, timing, and outcome.

entities_not_yet_in_schema.name: Skills
entities_not_yet_in_schema.description: Reusable agent capabilities. 62 skills defined across 10 agents in projection code. Not persisted in any DB table.

entities_not_yet_in_schema.name: AgentConfigs
entities_not_yet_in_schema.description: Persistent agent configuration including soul document references, capability declarations, and governance constraints. Currently agents are defined in Python code only.

entities_not_yet_in_schema.name: Metrics
entities_not_yet_in_schema.description: Business-level KPI tracking. Currently KPIs are defined in entities.py (per department) but not persisted in any DB table. KPIView queries the events table for ad-hoc calculation.

entities_not_yet_in_schema.name: MemoryObjects
entities_not_yet_in_schema.description: Persistent business context memory for agents. Onboarding seeds initial memory. Agents maintain context over time. Currently memory is in UMH substrate (not EOS-specific table).

entities_not_yet_in_schema.name: KnowledgeGraph
entities_not_yet_in_schema.description: Semantic relationship graph for business knowledge. End-state feature. Embeddings table provides vector storage but no graph structure exists.

entities_not_yet_in_schema.name: UniversalBusinessPrimitives
entities_not_yet_in_schema.description: Type instances for the 16 universal business primitive categories from the EOS ontology. Would store domain-specific typed records (e.g., offers, products, customer segments, channels).
entities_not_yet_in_schema.note: May not need a dedicated table -- could be a polymorphic design using the KnowledgeGraph or a JSONB column on the entity. Requires operator decision on storage strategy.

enums.name: org_plan

enums.name: complexity_level

rls_policy.target: org_id scoped row-level security on all tables
rls_policy.current_state: No RLS policies exist in any schema surface. Multi-tenancy is enforced only by application-level WHERE clauses (user_id in GitHub main, org_id in UMH platform).
rls_policy.desired_state: All tables scoped by org_id with RLS policies. Neon supports pg RLS natively. Clerk JWT includes org_id claim that maps to RLS policy variable.

implementation_options.description: Use Neon's built-in RLS support. Set current_setting from Clerk JWT org_id claim. All queries automatically filtered.
cons: Need to add org_id to all GitHub main tables first

implementation_options.description: All queries include WHERE org_id = ? at the application layer. No database-level RLS.
pros: No migration needed for existing tables
cons: Every query must remember to filter

rls_policy.recommendation: Neon RLS with Clerk JWT for production. Application-level for MVP with RLS migration before multi-tenant launch.

embedding_config.details: UMH platform schema defines embeddings as vector(384) using BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 (local model, no API cost). Desired state targets 1536 dimensions (OpenAI embedding models). Changing dimensions requires re-embedding all existing vectors. 384d local model is sufficient for MVP. 1536d provides better semantic resolution for knowledge graph end-state.
embedding_config.decision_needed: Keep 384d local model for MVP cost efficiency, or migrate to 1536d for better semantic quality? Can start with 384d and re-embed later, but migration is non-trivial.

from_github_to_beast.strategy: Beast branch (feature/company-system) is the canonical promotion candidate per DEC-145-001. Migration is from GitHub main schema to Beast schema, not the reverse.
prerequisites: Build validation on Beast branch (npm build, typecheck, lint)
Secret scan (no API keys, tokens, or credentials in code)
Schema comparison (diff Beast shared/schema.ts vs GitHub shared/schema.ts)
Data migration plan for any existing production data in ep_winter_sea
Rollback plan (GitHub main preserved as fallback branch)

schema_changes_needed.note: UMH platform uses uuid PKs. GitHub main uses text PKs. Beast likely uses text (same base). This must be resolved in unified schema.

schema_changes_needed.change: Add org_id to all EOS tables
schema_changes_needed.note: Required for multi-tenant isolation. Currently all tables use user_id for ownership. org_id adds organizational scoping.
Required for multi-entity support within an organization.

schema_changes_needed.change: Auth migration: remove Passport.js/Firebase, add Clerk
schema_changes_needed.note: Beast already has Clerk. This applies to GitHub main data migration.

schema_changes_needed.change: Merge Messages and AiMessages into unified Messages table
schema_changes_needed.note: Add thread_type discriminator (agent_conversation, ea_chat, copilot). Preserve all existing data.

schema_changes_needed.change: Create missing tables from Beast additions
schema_changes_needed.note: New tables, no migration of existing data needed.
agent_actions.requires_approval (GitHub main) and approvals table (UMH platform) serve overlapping purposes. Agent actions should reference the approvals table for governance gates.

neon_database_migration.strategy: Validate on ep_dark_poetry first. Cutover ep_winter_sea after validation.
neon_database_migration.v1_to_v2_changes: v1 has companies, crm_contacts, crm_deals, agent_actions, pipeline_runs. v2 uses events-driven architecture with umh_status columns and umh_outcomes table.

open_questions.question: Embedding dimension: keep 384d (BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5, free, local) or migrate to 1536d (OpenAI, paid, better quality)?
open_questions.impact: Affects knowledge graph quality, semantic search accuracy, and operational cost
open_questions.recommendation: 384d for MVP. Migrate to 1536d when knowledge graph is prioritized.

open_questions.question: RLS strategy: database-level (Neon RLS + Clerk JWT) or application-level (WHERE org_id = ?) for MVP?
open_questions.impact: Data isolation guarantees, security posture, implementation complexity
open_questions.recommendation: Application-level for MVP speed. Database-level before multi-tenant launch.

open_questions.question: Primary key type: text (GitHub main / Beast pattern) or uuid (UMH platform pattern)?
open_questions.impact: Cross-surface foreign keys, join performance, client-side ID generation
open_questions.recommendation: uuid for all new tables. Migrate existing text PKs to uuid during Beast promotion.

open_questions.question: How does the Entities table relate to the Organizations table? Are they the same thing, or does an Organization contain multiple Entities?
open_questions.impact: Fundamental data model for multi-entity portfolio management
open_questions.recommendation: Organization IS the Entity container. One Organization = one legal entity. Portfolio contains multiple Organizations. Add entity_type, jurisdiction, formation_date to organizations table.

open_questions.question: Should Business Primitives be a dedicated table or JSONB columns on existing entities?
open_questions.recommendation: Start with JSONB on entities for MVP. Promote to dedicated table if query patterns demand it.

open_questions.question: Beast branch schema is not directly inspectable from VPS. Should Beast be pulled to VPS for exact schema diff before any migration planning?
open_questions.recommendation: Yes. Pull Beast shared/schema.ts to VPS for exact comparison before implementation.

open_questions.question: Unified events table (v2 architecture in ep_dark_poetry) vs normalized tables (v1 in ep_winter_sea). Which is canonical?
open_questions.impact: Data architecture direction, query patterns, UMH integration surface
open_questions.recommendation: Events table for UMH integration (signals, outcomes). Normalized tables for direct CRUD. Both coexist.

relationship_summary.description: Complete relationship map across all EOS entities.
relationship_summary.hierarchy_chain: User -> Portfolio -> Organization/Entity -> Department -> Role -> Agent
relationship_summary.execution_chain: Workflow -> WorkflowRun -> Task -> AgentAction -> Approval -> UmhOutcome
cross_cutting: Agent connects to: Tasks (assignment), Messages (conversation), CrmDeals (assignment), CrmActivities (creation), AgentActions (execution), AgentMetrics (measurement)
User connects to: everything via ownership (user_id FK), Organizations via OrgMembers, Approvals via resolved_by
Organization scopes: Approvals, UmhOutcomes, UserAgentSessions, Embeddings, and (desired state) all EOS business tables
